cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and what the change made has settled into something you can hold.
cells.ask: Name one thing the change produced that you are keeping, hand a piece of it to someone today, and hold the rest.
cells.core:
Something got made and you can feel its edges. You see the whole shape from where you stand — outside it and still in it — and you know what is worth keeping and what can go. None of this is hoarding. You are carrying what the clearing left behind.

The pattern is read; now it holds. The one thing to watch is that holding and giving are not the same motion. What you have is free to feed into exchange — the kind that leaves you level, not emptied out. So say the thing out loud to one person. Let what you carry be visible to somebody besides you, and see what comes back.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a change that hasn't arrived yet, guarding a shape that may not need guarding.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are protecting tonight, set it down where it can be seen, and leave it there until tomorrow.
cells.core:
You see the whole pattern and you are already ahead of it. What is coming, what might undo what you built, what the next change will take — you have run it, and you are gripping tighter than this moment calls for. Keeping it safe has become the work, and the work is a guess about a future nobody can hand you.

What you see is not wrong. It is just spending itself on tomorrow, and the thing you built is not being lived in. What you are protecting wants a kind of attention you can give it — real contact, not control. So set one thing down where somebody else can see it. If it stands on its own, you learn what was yours to carry. You do not have to keep it away from people to keep it.

cells.tense: Something was made and you are still standing at the door where it happened, holding none of it.
cells.ask: Choose the direction you feel pulled toward and take one step this week that a camera could see — without explaining it to anyone first.
cells.core:
The change happened and you are not close to what it made. You can still read the pattern, but from a distance, and nothing in front of you feels like yours. That is not a shortage of feeling. The part of you that moves from what it feels is running on empty.

So the way back is not more feeling, and it is not pushing yourself to care about the shape. It is direction. Take one thing you would move toward if you let yourself, and move toward it. Clear sight comes back when something of yours is in motion. One step, taken from what you actually want, and the door stops being the place you live.
cells.sheetLine: You saw what the change made. Acting on one direction brings you back into it.

cells.tense: You are already holding the shape steady for the people around you, and you keep calling it the situation.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that one thing you are keeping steady is your doing — then let someone else hold part of it.
cells.core:
You are keeping something steady and you have not put your name on it. People bring you the pieces, you see the whole shape, and things come to rest around you — and you describe it as if that just happened, or as if anyone would do it. It does not just happen. Your read of the pattern is what holds it together.

That is the quiet part of preservation: it works when nobody marks it. But keeping it has a cost, and the cost is being paid by someone who has not said they are paying it. So name one thing out loud. Not a speech — one piece of steadiness. Then let somebody else keep a part of it for a while. Structure you claim can be shared. Structure you disown has to stay yours.
cells.sheetLine: You are the one holding it steady. Say so, then let it be shared.

attempts.check: The record supports Preservation as Transformation through Structure seated in Recognition, with the four medicines named; what it does not support is any claim about what the person has actually been through — so Too Little must locate the capacity that stopped without saying what room it stopped in or who was there. A reader could reasonably object that no one is this tidy about holding what a change produced, or that Recognition and Preservation are the same act — the cell has to keep them distinct: one sees the pattern, the other keeps what the seeing and the change produced. The ask survives being wrong because it is an act, not a diagnosis — a camera could see it, and it does not depend on my read of their history. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any line that admires the holding itself; I have cut that and left the cost of keeping it in the open.
